definitions: A type of catalysis in which a chiral catalyst converts an achiral or prochiral substrate into a chiral product, typically with a high enantiomeric excess.
The process of synthesizing chiral compounds using a catalyst that favors the formation of one enantiomer over the other.
examples: Asymmetric catalysis is crucial in pharmaceutical synthesis.
The development of new methods for asymmetric catalysis is an active research area.
Many industrial processes rely on efficient asymmetric catalysis.
